content.title: 2026 Masters full TV schedule for this week
content.text: Scottie Scheffler walks to green on the 13th hole during a practice round ahead of the Masters golf tournament at the Augusta National Golf Club, Monday, April 6, 2026, in Augusta, Ga.(AP Photo/Matt Slocum)If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Thomas Lagrone | tlagrone@al.comThe 2026 Masters is scheduled to begin this week, as round 1 coverage starts Thursday morning. The prestigious golf tournament will conclude on Sunday, and the coverage will be televised on these networks: Prime Video, ESPN, Paramount+, and CBS. Can you watch the 2026 Masters for free this week?Fans can watch almost all of the 2026 Masters for free online this week, as free trials are available for three of the four networks: ESPN, CBS, and Prime Video. DIRECTV and Fubo TV offer free trials to new users, while also carrying ESPN and CBS. Golf fans can also watch all of the action on Prime Video with a free trial.Does Paramount+ offer a free trial to watch the 2026 Masters?The only network that does not offer a free trial to watch the 2026 Masters is Paramount+. Golf fans will need to purchase a monthly subscription for $8.99 to watch part of the tournament. 2026 Masters full schedule:Thursday, April 9 (Round 1)12-2 p.m. CT on Prime Video2-6:30 p.m. CT on ESPNFriday, April 10 (Round 2)12-2 p.m. CT on Prime Video2-6:30 p.m. CT on ESPNSaturday, April 11 (Round 3)11-1 p.m. CT on Paramount+1-6 p.m. CT on Paramount+/CBSSunday, April 12 (Final Round)11-1 p.m. CT on Paramount+1-6 p.m. CT on Paramount+/CBS Related: Win a $5 live bet on the Masters, get $300 bonus today with latest DraftKings promoWhere to watch Dodgers-Mets MLB game for free todayWhere to watch Clippers vs. Warriors NBA Play-In Tournament for free todayWhere to watch Yankees vs. Angels MLB game for free todayHow to watch 76ers vs. Magic NBA Play-In Tournament for free todayWhere to watch Arsenal vs. Sporting CP leg 2 Champions League Quarterfinal livestream todayThomas Lagrone is an Alabama native and recent graduate from the University of Alabama at Birmingham with a bachelor's degree in sports communication.
